hold.example: Hold on a second — I'll be right back
She tried to hold back her tears
Traffic held us up for almost an hour

hold.meaning: resistir; durar; esperar por algo melhor
hold.pattern: hold out / hold out for + noun
hold.example: They held out for a better offer
hold.note: hold out for = recusar enquanto espera algo melhor

keep.pattern: keep up / keep up with + noun
keep.example: It's hard to keep up with all the changes
keep.note: keep up with someone = acompanhar o ritmo

keep.example: He kept on asking the same question
keep.note: Semelhante a keep + -ing, com ênfase em continuidade

keep.meaning: manter-se afastado ou manter algo longe
keep.note: Com objeto: keep children away from the fire

keep.example: Keep the door closed to keep the noise out
The police kept the crowd back
keep.note: Menos comum que hold back, mas útil em controle físico

leave.example: You left an important detail out of the report
I left my umbrella behind at the café
Let's continue from where we left off yesterday
leave.note: Muito comum na expressão where we left off

let.example: I don't want to let the team down
Can you let the dog in?
She let the cat out before breakfast
let.note: Também: let out a scream = soltar um grito

let.meaning: não punir ou punir levemente; liberar
let.example: The teacher let him off with a warning

look.example: Can you look after the kids for an hour?
The company is looking into the complaint
Could you look over this email before I send it?
look.note: Pode ser separável: look it over

look.example: I looked the address up online

look.pattern: look out / look out for + noun
look.example: Look out! There's a car coming
look.note: look out for something = ficar atento a algo

make.pattern: make + story/excuse + up / make up with + person
make.example: He made up an excuse for being late
make.note: Também: make up with someone = fazer as pazes

make.example: I couldn't make out what he was saying
make.note: Também usado em outros sentidos informais; contexto é importante

make.meaning: dirigir-se a; contribuir para um resultado
make.example: As soon as it started raining, we made for the car
make.note: Também: Good lighting makes for a better workspace

move.note: Com destino: move into a new apartment

move.pattern: move out / move out of + place
move.example: He moved out of the apartment last month
move.note: Use move out of antes do lugar

move.meaning: seguir adiante ou passar para outro assunto
move.pattern: move on / move on to + topic/stage
move.example: Let's move on to the next question
move.note: Muito comum em reuniões e apresentações

move.example: Could you move over a little?

move.meaning: subir de posição, nível ou lugar
move.pattern: move up / move up to + level
move.example: She moved up to a management role last year

pass.example: Her grandfather passed away last winter
pass.note: Forma mais suave e indireta de dizer die

pass.example: He nearly passed out from the heat
pass.note: Com objeto: pass the forms out

pass.example: Please pass the message on to everyone
pass.note: Também: I'll pass on dessert = vou recusar

pass.example: I couldn't pass up the chance to travel
pass.note: Não é separável na prática com esses objetos

pass.example: He was passed over for promotion again
pass.note: Muito comum na voz passiva: be passed over for

pull.example: The police officer asked me to pull over
I don't know how they pulled off the event in two weeks

pull.meaning: sobreviver ou se recuperar de situação difícil
pull.example: The doctors think he'll pull through
The company pulled out of the deal

pull.pattern: pull back / pull back from + noun
pull.example: The company pulled back from the expansion plan

push.pattern: push + object + back / push back against + noun
push.example: They pushed the deadline back by a week

push.meaning: forçar aprovação ou concluir apesar de dificuldade
push.example: They pushed the proposal through despite strong opposition
We were tired, but we decided to push on

put.meaning: colocar no chão, abaixar ou deixar algo em uma superfície
put.example: Put the box down next to the door
put.note: Com pronome: put it down, não put down it

put.meaning: guardar ou colocar de volta no lugar
put.example: Please put the dishes away after dinner
She put in three hours of overtime yesterday
put.note: Muito comum com time, effort, work e instalações

put.example: Put your jacket on before you go outside
put.note: Com pronome: put it on; também pode significar ligar um aparelho ou música

put.meaning: adiar; em outro uso, causar rejeição ou desânimo
put.example: They put the meeting off until Friday
put.note: Com pronome: put it off; put someone off = desanimar ou causar rejeição

put.meaning: apagar fogo/luz; também disponibilizar ou publicar
put.example: Please put the candle out before you leave

put.meaning: levantar, instalar ou colocar algo em posição
put.example: They put up a new shelf in the kitchen
put.note: Também: put someone up = hospedar alguém temporariamente

put.meaning: devolver ao lugar ou adiar para uma data posterior
put.example: Put the milk back in the fridge when you're done
